stimuli.description: An open-plan office environment modified to laboratory-like conditions, including ceiling-high sound screens and acoustic panels, indirect lighting, and furniture.

Twelve different sound conditions: silence, unmasked speech, and ten masked speech conditions. Masked speech varied by SNR (-9 dB or -12 dB), masker location (same direction, 90° different direction, or conventional ceiling), and masker HPF (100 Hz or 200 Hz). Speech signals were German sentences from two studio monitors (T1, T2). Masking sounds were filtered pink noise from local emitters (M1, M2) or conventional ceiling emitters (M0).

limitations: The study was performed in an open-plan office with state-of-the-art acoustical design, but with room-high partitions, making it not comparable to a conventional open-plan office.
The direct and reverberant components reaching a worker, and thus sound fields, may differ notably between this office and conventional open offices.
The distances of the speech sources (3-4 m) were relatively small, which might be too short for effective sound masking or where communication is desired.

The study considered only sound conditions with one disturbing background speech signal with a single voice, whereas multi-talker environments are more realistic and may impair working memory performance differently.
The setup did not allow for a separation of the effects of speech and sound masking loudspeaker locations in multi-talker environments.
